resources.string: Relative transfer = relative area × relative pressure difference ÷ relative thickness.

All inputs are multiples of a synthetic baseline. This plane-layer example holds oxygen diffusivity constant and omits blood flow and hemoglobin binding. It does not estimate blood oxygen or clinical lung function.
Alveolar air → exchange barrier → capillary blood
Compressive strain (percent) = 100 × stress ÷ modulus, using the same units for both.

A small-strain, uniform elastic example of articular cartilage. It omits fluid transport, time dependence and tissue layers. This models tissue, not an individual chondrocyte, and does not estimate injury or joint health.
Articular cartilage before and under load. Deformation enlarged.
In this model, outer stress = moment × outer radius ÷ second moment of area.

A hollow circular beam with synthetic dimensions. Actual bones are irregular, with different properties across and along their length. These stresses do not predict bone strength, fracture risk, or safe exercise loads.
Example bone cross section and stress across its depth.
